newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea to let banks cash in repos early.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea to let banks cash in repos early.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) has decided to allow banks to cash in 489 billion won worth of repurchase agreements (Repos) on Friday, five days ahead of their original maturity, a BOK official said.
The move would effectively inject 489 billion won in emergency funds into the banking system.
"It is aimed at easing the expected shortages of daily reserve requirement levels at banks," said the BOK official.
Cash liquidity has been tightening in the aftermath of the financial crisis at the Kia Group, which was offered protection this week by its creditors.
One of the group's creditor banks, the Korea First Bank , said on Tuesday it had selected for bail-out 18 Kia affiliates, including flagship Kia Motors Corp.
